Gerah
GAY-rah
n. (Hebrew)
Hebrew gērāh, probably from a root meaning a grain or small object; the smallest weight unit in the Hebrew system, equal to 1/20 of a shekel of the sanctuary (approximately 0.02 oz / 0.57 g of silver).

📖 Biblical Definition

The gerah is the smallest weight unit in the Hebrew system—1/20 of a shekel of the sanctuary, mentioned five times in the OT exclusively as the precise standard for measuring half-shekel, shekel, and larger weights. Exodus 30:13 prescribes the standard: this they shall give, every one that passeth among them that are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary: (a shekel is twenty gerahs:) an half shekel shall be the offering of the LORD. The gerah-standard is mentioned similarly in Lev 27:25; Num 3:47; 18:16; and Ezek 45:12 (Ezekiel’s prophetic temple vision specifies the standard with reference to the gerah). The structural significance of the gerah is twofold. First, the precision of biblical weights: the OT does not deal in approximations but in precisely-standardized units. The shekel of the sanctuary was a specific weight (the temple-standard), and it was reckoned in exactly twenty gerahs. The Israelite buying, selling, paying tribute, weighing-out atonement money knew exactly what a shekel weighed because the standard was set in the most easily-verifiable terms (twenty units of the smallest standard weight). Second, the smallness as standard: the smallest unit of the system was the basis of the larger units’ precision. By specifying that one shekel equals twenty gerahs, the LORD ensured that every shekel-payment could be checked against the verifiable smaller standard, and that no merchant or priest could manipulate the larger units without violating the smaller ones. The biblical-pastoral application of the gerah-precision is the wider biblical theology of just weights and measures, which the prophets repeatedly emphasize. Leviticus 19:35-36: ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in meteyard, in weight, or in measure. Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall ye have: I am the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt. Proverbs 11:1: a false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight. Proverbs 20:10: divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to the LORD. Amos 8:5 condemns merchants who make the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsify the balances by deceit. Micah 6:11: shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights? The gerah-standard’s precision is the basis of the prophetic ethics: the LORD’s holiness requires that every weight be just, every measure exact, every commercial transaction honest—and the very precision-standardization of the OT weights-and-measures system (with the small gerah as the verifying base) is the structural infrastructure on which the prophetic ethics depends.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

(Hebrew term.) GERAH: the smallest weight in the Hebrew system, equal to 1/20 of a shekel of the sanctuary; the precision-standard against which all larger weights were measured; basis of the OT theology of just weights and measures that the prophets repeatedly emphasize.

GERAH, n. — (Hebrew weight.) The smallest weight in the Hebrew system, equal to 1/20 of a shekel of the sanctuary (Ex 30:13; Lev 27:25; Num 3:47; 18:16; Ezek 45:12).

WEIGHTS AND MEASURES — The biblical doctrine of just commercial standards, prescribed in Lev 19:35-36 and Deut 25:13-16, condemned in their corruption by the prophets (Amos 8:5; Mic 6:11; Hos 12:7), and grounded in the LORD’s holiness against deceitful commerce.

📖 Key Scripture

Exodus 30:13 — "This they shall give, every one that passeth among them that are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary: (a shekel is twenty gerahs:) an half shekel shall be the offering of the LORD."

Leviticus 19:35-36 — "Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in meteyard, in weight, or in measure. Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall ye have: I am the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt."

Proverbs 11:1 — "A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight."

Amos 8:5 — "Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The gerah-doctrine is corrupted chiefly by the general loss of biblical-economic ethics in much contemporary preaching, which has muted the prophetic-and-Mosaic emphasis on just weights and measures that the gerah-precision-standard underwrites; the doctrine’s recovery is the recovery of the biblical theology of honest commerce as part of the LORD’s holiness against the deceitful trading patterns of every age including the present.

expand to see more

The general loss of biblical-economic ethics in much contemporary preaching has muted the OT and prophetic emphasis on just weights and measures, of which the gerah-precision-standard is the structural foundation. The prophetic literature thunders against deceitful balances, divers weights, false measures, the making-of-the-ephah-small-and-the-shekel-great pattern of contemporary commerce. The contemporary application is direct: every age has its forms of deceitful commerce—tampered measures, misleading advertising, hidden fees, manipulated invoices, false labeling, deceptive pricing, fraudulent accounting—and the LORD’s holiness against these is no less than His holiness against the OT merchants who falsified the balances. The Christian businessman, accountant, contractor, employee, employer is bound by the same ethics that the gerah-standard underwrote in OT Israel: every weight just, every measure exact, every transaction honest, every account truly stated. The recovery is the recovery of biblical-economic ethics as part of the saint’s discipleship, with the gerah-precision-standard as the OT figure of the precision-honesty God’s holiness requires in commerce.

The deeper pastoral substance is that the LORD’s holiness extends into every detail of human life, including the smallest units of commercial measurement. The gerah was the smallest unit in the Hebrew system, and the LORD specified the larger units in terms of the smallest—ensuring that no manipulation of the larger could escape verification by the smaller. Applied today: the saint’s honesty is to extend to the smallest details of his financial life. The integrity of the larger transactions is built on the integrity of the smaller. The believer who is honest in the visible large transactions and dishonest in the small (the petty cash, the expense report, the under-the-table payment, the unreported income) has corrupted the whole, because the LORD’s holiness extends to the smallest unit and no commercial integrity is real that does not begin at the gerah-level. The contemporary recovery is the recovery of comprehensive financial integrity, all the way down to the smallest units, as part of the discipleship that responds to the holiness of the God who set the weights and measures of His people with such precision.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew gērāh (smallest weight, 1/20 shekel of the sanctuary); five OT uses, all in precision-standard contexts (Ex 30:13; Lev 27:25; Num 3:47; 18:16; Ezek 45:12); the precision-standard against which all larger weights were measured; basis of the OT theology of just weights and measures emphasized by the prophets and Mosaic law alike.

expand to see more

Hebrew gērāh (H1626) — gerah, 1/20 shekel (5 OT uses, all precision-standard).

Hebrew sheqel ha-qōdesh — shekel of the sanctuary (the standard reckoned in 20 gerahs).

Hebrew mō’znē tsedeq — just balances (the prophetic-and-Mosaic standard of commercial honesty).

Greek stathō-cognates — weighing-related Greek terms (the NT continues the principle of just commerce; e.g., Eph 4:28’s command against stealing).

"Loss of biblical-economic ethics mutes the prophetic emphasis; recovery is the comprehensive financial integrity that extends to the smallest units, as the LORD’s holiness requires."
